clue.text: Paper round?

definitions.meaning: a printed notice or leaflet sent out to many people
shaped like a ring or disc

explanation.surface: A newspaper delivery route, the job of many a teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the single phrase 'paper round', a newspaper delivery job; split it and each word is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet mailed to many households is called by that name, and the same word is the adjective for anything ring-shaped.

clue.text: Caught, as about to steal trees

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a is a recognised short form of about, as in dates
robs means steals from

explanation.surface: Someone is caught just as they are about to steal from an orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediterranean evergreens whose pods give a chocolate substitute.

clue.text: Leave job and enter into another contract

definitions.meaning: to put your name to an agreement again

explanation.surface: An employee quits one job and signs up for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as RE-SIGN, signing again.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a post, or, split with a hyphen, to sign a renewed agreement.

clue.text: Not charged, due to duodenal trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of duodenal are disturbed

explanation.surface: A person not charged by police because of a stomach problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges DUODENAL; 'due to' is a link. 'charged' looks legal but means a gun not loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with no cartridge in it is not charged.

clue.text: Official proceedings partly play on one

parts.note: an act is a part of a play
a means one

explanation.surface: Records of a play put on for one performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural for recorded deeds, the minutes of an official body.

clue.text: Monkey showing liveliness on tree-top

parts.note: verve means energy, spirit, liveliness

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so tree gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A lively monkey perched at the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tree-top' looks like one word for the place the monkey sits, but 'top' picks the first letter of 'tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small African guenon with a black face, a species of primate.

clue.text: Versatile stance needed when one performs here

indicators.note: versatile suggests the letters of stance can take many forms

explanation.surface: A flexible posture is needed when an actor takes the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Versatile' rearranges STANCE; 'needed when one' and 'here' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a role or play is to perform it.

clue.text: Random vetting has point, but the result's somewhat sketchy

indicators.note: random means the letters of vetting are put in no particular order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Random vetting has a purpose but produces vague results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Random' rearranges VETTING into VIGNETT, then E (east) is added; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief descriptive sketch or small illustration is a short, partial piece.

clue.text: Agreements reached on different rate restrictions

indicators.note: reached is taken as getting in among, so the reworked letters arrive inside the restrictions

parts.note: ties are bonds that restrict

indicators.note: different suggests the letters of rate are made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: Treaties reached on new interest rate limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrictions' sounds like rules but means ties, bonds that hold something back; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal pacts between nations are agreements.

clue.text: Rose playing musical instrument with determination

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: acting with determination is acting firmly

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of rose are put into play, rearranged

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose plays her instrument with grim determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges ROSE into RESO; 'Rose' looks like a name, or a flower, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm in purpose and unwavering shows determination in everything they do.

clue.text: Knotted mass of seaweed

definitions.meaning: a snarl of twisted strands, as of hair or string
a large brown kelp of the genus Laminaria has this name

explanation.surface: A knotted clump of seaweed washed up on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl of string is the everyday sense; the word is also a name for kelp, a coarse brown marine alga.

clue.text: Wager half back-track soon

parts.note: bet means wager

indicators.note: back signals the word for half is read backwards

parts.note: semi means half, as in semicircle

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on half the course, then retraces his steps early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SEMI, a prefix meaning half, giving IMES; 'track' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning early or in good time.

clue.text: Poor fellow, he has no choice

definitions.meaning: an impoverished man who asks for alms
from the proverb that such people cannot be choosers

explanation.surface: Pity the poor man who has no say in the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition rests on the saying 'beggars can't be choosers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper who lives on alms, and, by the proverb, someone who cannot pick and choose.

clue.text: Let beast loose? Restraint needed!

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters of let beast are set free and scattered

explanation.surface: If you let an animal loose, you will need to restrain it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges LET BEAST; the surface's restraint for a beast becomes a car safety strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap holding a passenger in a car seat is a safety restraint.

clue.text: A number still in the pen

indicators.note: in places the word for still inside the pen

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
even as an adjective means still or calm

explanation.surface: A count of animals still kept in the enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten times seven, a cardinal number.

clue.text: It's good for you to have a change from endless tinned beef hash

indicators.note: a hash is a jumble of chopped food, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: read as end-less: the three letters of the word end are what the mix goes without

explanation.surface: A plate of tinned corned beef hash, which is supposedly good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: TINNED BEEF holds the answer's letters plus E, N and D; 'endless' says to go without those, and 'hash' mixes the rest. 'to have a change from' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage or gain is something that does you good.

clue.text: Near-sighted gathering

parts.note: not a myopic crowd but a gathering of pus sitting near the organ of sight, an eyelid swelling

explanation.surface: A meeting of short-sighted people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near-sighted' looks like myopic, and 'gathering' like a meeting; medically a gathering is a pus-filled swelling, and this one is near the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a boil-like gathering beside the eye.

clue.text: Clan turned out in a little bay, for meeting

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged clan inside the little bay

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters of clan are reshaped

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan gathers in a small bay for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little bay' looks descriptive, but it is the whole definition of the outer word; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A private assembly, especially of cardinals choosing a pope.

clue.text: Unlimited credit, so they say, around the North? That's mad!

indicators.note: around means the sounded-out letters go about the north
so they say marks a homophone: the phrase is spoken to give the letters

parts.note: free tick: tick is credit, and free credit is unlimited
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Endless credit up north, people claim, is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so they say' turns FREE TICK into a sound, spelt FREETIC; 'around' puts N inside it. 'tick' is British slang for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildly agitated and frenzied, as if crazed.

clue.text: Perhaps I lost a stone

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters of perhaps I have gone astray

explanation.surface: A rueful admission that maybe I mislaid a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges PERHAPS I.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious blue gemstone, a kind of corundum.

clue.text: A fearsome character — therefore, turned back

indicators.note: turned back signals the word for therefore is read in reverse

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A frightening figure, so the travellers turned back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses ERGO, the Latin word for 'therefore'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monstrous giant of fairy tales, or a frightening person.

clue.text: Reveals mix-up to more than one

indicators.note: a mix-up means the letters of reveals are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled disclosure gets passed to more people than intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix-up' rearranges REVEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A determiner meaning a few, some, more than a couple.

clue.text: This flower occurs all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters of occurs are scattered

explanation.surface: A flower that grows everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges OCCURS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-blooming corm of the iris family.

clue.text: Fire, when set far off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of set far are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Shoot when the target is set far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET FAR; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft is to shoot at.

clue.text: Computers that slither about?

definitions.meaning: people or machines that compute sums, totting figures up
snakes, the venomous vipers of Britain

explanation.surface: Computers that crawl along, as slow as snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as add-ers, things that add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that add figures, and also European vipers, which slither.

clue.text: Credit note newsman dropped somehow — sorry outcome

indicators.note: dropped says the letters of the newsman are left out of the mix
somehow suggests the remaining letters come out in some other order

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword newsman

explanation.surface: A credit note lost by a journalist leads to an apology.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: CREDIT NOTE holds the answer's letters plus ED, the editor; 'dropped' removes those and the anagram signal rearranges the rest. 'outcome' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitent and remorseful, feeling regret for a wrong done.

clue.text: Ran round it when thwarted

indicators.note: round says the word for ran goes around it

parts.note: sped means ran or hurried

explanation.surface: Someone ran in circles after being thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' looks like the main verb of the surface but only supplies letters; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite as a verb means to frustrate or annoy someone deliberately, so spited means blocked out of malice.

clue.text: Girl in overalls

indicators.note: in signals the name is hidden inside the word overalls

explanation.surface: A girl dressed in overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is hidden in 'oVERAlls'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name.

clue.text: Launch an assault, invoking strong criticism

definitions.meaning: to set upon an enemy with force
a sharp verbal onslaught against a person or idea

explanation.surface: A critic opens fire with a scathing review.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging an enemy is one sense; a fierce verbal broadside is the other.

clue.text: Think partner is getting to grips with new diet

indicators.note: getting to grips with means holding on to, so the partner grips the other letters inside

parts.note: a mate is a partner or spouse

indicators.note: new signals the letters of diet arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Contemplate your spouse's struggle with a new diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partner' looks like a business colleague, but in crosswords a mate is the usual partner; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or reflect deeply, a quiet form of thinking.

clue.text: Pardon for former copper at commencement of sentence

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the commencement of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A former police officer seeks a pardon at the start of his prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal: CU is its chemical symbol. 'commencement of' takes the first letter of 'sentence'.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgive or overlook a fault is to let it go.

clue.text: To demonstrate affection, embracing the Parisian is imprudent

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to caress is to stroke someone tenderly
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Showing affection by hugging a Frenchman is unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Parisian' is a common crossword way to ask for a French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless and incautious, acting without due thought.
